questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academically: I do a MSc in political science with specialization in IR and conflict resolution, and Uniandes is well-known for its Master program and courses in this relation. Personally: my boyfriend is Colombian and living in Bogota.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall I would say that the experience was good, however, getting the courses I had hoped for, unfortunately, turned out to be challenging. The Covid situation also made stuff a bit challenging since most of my classes turned out to be online.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The uni sends you a lot of e-mails with all the info you need.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: In the week before the classes started you had two online info meetings and an in-person campus tour.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was good. The info was pretty clear and well-prepared for the students, even though most of it were online.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: This did not specifically apply to me given that I stayed at my boyfriend's place, but there is a lot of student housing that is offered to students close to the campus area.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The traffic in the city messy, so stay in a place more or less close to uni. Also as a master student I had classes either very early in the morning or in the late afternoon, so it was also practical to live close to campus because of this.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Does not apply to be, but it seems to be good.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: To accept the place was easy, but to registrer for courses were more challenging even though you receive most of the info you need. Important to read all info before starting the latter process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They had two different portals to apply for courses through depending on possible course restrictions.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could ask for help over e-mail or through a Teams groups that was created for the international coordinators and the students. This worked well, and the coordinators answered fast.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately in this relation I was not very lucky. I only ended up with one out of three courses that I initially had hoped for. Despite applying just after the application portals had opened I ended up getting rejected from most of the courses I really wanted, and actually had to contact the international coordination office. They managed to fix me one, so I was happy with that.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for many more courses than you need. I needed three and applied for five (in which I was advised), but since it took time before I heard back on the courses, a lot of other courses that could have worked as second options were already gone when I had to apply for others.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was pretty satisfied, but actually thought that there would have been some more options. I do not know if that might have been due to the covid situation.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was good. I was challenged academically in at least two out of three courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Way more oral presentations, and also more work throughout the semester and not only one exam or paper to hand in by the end of the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Populism in global perspective, religion and politics and war and peace in the voices of their protagonists.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend them all depending on your specific interests. They all had interesting elements. Particularly did I enjoy the populism course due to an excellent visiting professor from Canada.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing that I can think of.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Colombia is pretty cheap, so nothing. Prices are good. Especially cabs and food are cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Uniandes is a private university and has a lot to offer in this relation.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a lot to offer in every sense, however, some natural restrictions due to covid.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not participate regularly on anything and was little on campus due to the covid situation and most of my classes being online.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Bogota has a lot to offer for everyone. Many great restaurants, hikes in the mountains around, etc. Monserrate is a must.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, but I had also been in the city on several occasions before doing my exchange semester in Bogota. I guess it depends on how much experience you have from Latin American countries and big cities before coming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be active and get engaged in activities that are offered through the university. There was also a group of local students that helped organizing trips and activities of different kinds for exchange students. However, some stuff was obviously restricted due to the covid situation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How friendly and overall helpful the locals are. Food is also great.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be as open and adaptable as possible, and do not expect things to be done the same ways that you might be used to from DK.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know new people, experience the Colombian way of doing thing in general, and also, and especially, getting a different perspective on academic stuff.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Covid. I barely had classes on campus and most of my classes were online.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
